Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Dragon Castle concise reference by hecose Setup: • Board – 1 Spirit card, 1 Dragon card, fill countdown tokens according to #players, extras stacked on leftmost space. • Player – 1 shrine. Concepts: • Available tile = at least one long side not blocked. • Adjacent = orthogonally, not diagonally. Different levels OK. Turn: • 1 Mandatory Action: a) Take 1 tile from top floor, then exact matching tile from any floor. b) Take 1 tile from top floor and 1 shrine. c) Take 1 tile from top floor, then discard facedown for 1VP. d) Summon dragon. Allowed when only floor 1 tiles left. Claim rightmost countdown token (worth 2VP). Once exclamation mark revealed, play until end of round. • Put claimed tiles on own board, on free space or facedown tile, never on faceup tile or shrine. • If any 4+ adjacent tiles are of same colour, must consolidate by flipping facedown and scoring. • When consolidating, may build shrine from own pool onto newly consolidated tiles. Faction(red/green/yellow) tiles allow 1 shrine, Special tiles(blue/black) allow 2, Dragon tile(Purple) also gives 1VP. • 1 Optional Action: discard faceup tiles or shrine to activate Spirit power. Game end scoring: VP tokens collected Countdown tokens Dragon card objective Shrines score 1/2/3VP at floors 1/2/3+ Tiebreaker: most facedown stacks, then shrines Other notes: • For Spirit cards and Dragon cards, refer pages 12 – 15. # of tiles / VP 4 / 2 5 / 3 6 / 5 7 / 6 8 / 8 > 8 / +1 Board Game Arena would like to thank Horrible Guild for making it possible to have this game here. 1151 dragoncastle العربية беларуская мова български език Brezhoneg Català čeština Dansk Deutsch Ελληνικά English Español Eesti keel فارسی Suomi Français Galego עברית Hrvatski Magyar Italiano Bahasa Indonesia 日本語 한국어 Lietuvių Latviešu Bahasa Malaysia Nederlands Norsk Polski Português Română Русский язык Slovenčina Slovenščina Српски Svenska ไทย Türkçe Українська мова Tiếng Việt 中文 (漢) 中文 (汉) Application loading... ... {DISPLAY_IN_OTHER_LANG} {LANG_REDIRECT_CODE} boardgamearena.com Top Help What is Board Game Arena? [Rating: 1/10] There's a lot that should be appealing about this game, and I am a big fan of messing about with mahjong tiles. But the gameplay seems messy and arbitrary, under designed.

[Rating: 1/10] I've seen games suck before, but they were the suckiest bunch of sucks that ever sucked

[Rating: 1/10] Game about taking tiles and trying to make combos. Too draggy for me. Not my kind of game.

[Rating: 1/10] Just another dull solitaire take & make, the only thing remarkable about it is the use of mahjong tiles but this doesn't even include enough tiles to play riichi mahjong (which is a much better game than this) so no point in bothering with this.

[Rating: 2/10] I thought this game had some great looking artwork and components when I first played it on Board Game Arena, then I traded for a physical copy and I was blown away by how poor-quality the tiles are. Whoever accepted the production standards of this game had possibly never seen or felt a real Mahjong tile - the cheap plastic here was a million miles away from that. (Although perhaps this was an elaborate satire of the way that the grey plastic monstrosities in your average "dudes on a map" Kickstarter are simply a less enjoyable tactile experience than the wooden meeples of Carcasonne?) [Rating: 3/10] Played the game in Essen, my friend was about to buy the game when a table opened up, so we decided to play a quick round first, great decision because none of us liked the game, yes the stones are lovely, but the player papers and set up paper were very disappointing, gameplay didn't capture us at all, we actually stopped playing the game before we were done because we just couldn't care anymore.

[Rating: 3/10] They were tempting fate with the company name.  Nothing bad but absolutely dull as dull can be. No clever idea. No nothing.  An afternoon of design work.

[Rating: 3/10] Tedious.  There are so few restrictions on how to build your own stacks that the few existing limits are meaningless.  You can't mess up.  And there is so little information about the future that planning around the central castle is meaningless with more than 2 players.  You can't plan.  So you just do the obvious simple thing on your turn, then zone out until your next turn.  The gimmick of using MahJong tiles is wasted, and the tiles are low quality compared to most moderate-quality MahJong sets I've seen.  So, the aesthetic doesn't even really hit home.
